title: Refactor python_path_migration file_utils to use pathlib.Path
description: Brownfield Python refactor: replace os.path calls in src/file_utils.py with pathlib.Path equivalents. All 5 existing tests must still pass.

task_spec.prompt:
Refactor src/file_utils.py to use pathlib.Path instead of os.path.

Remove `import os` and replace with `from pathlib import Path`.

  def list_text_files(directory: str) -> list[str]:
    — use Path(directory).iterdir() to list files
    — check .is_file() and .suffix == '.txt'
    — return sorted list of .name strings

  def read_if_exists(path: str) -> str | None:
    — use Path(path).exists() and Path(path).read_text(encoding='utf-8')

  def ensure_dir(path: str) -> str:
    — use Path(path).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    — return path (the str, unchanged)

Do not modify the test file. All 5 tests must still pass.
Run: uv run pytest tests/ -v
required_artifacts: os import removed, pathlib.Path used instead
ensure_dir uses Path.mkdir with parents=True, exist_ok=True
success_criteria: uv run python -c "from src.file_utils import list_text_files, read_if_exists, ensure_dir" passes
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.

check_commands.build: uv run python -c "from src.file_utils import list_text_files, read_if_exists, ensure_dir"
